newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks slipped, but losses seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks slipped, but losses seen limited.

text.p: (0950 GMT) Madrid stocks slipped at the start on Thursday morning, pulled down by yesterday's negative close at Wall Street.

But dealers said the underlying tone of the domestic market remained positive, adding profit taking was limited in very light volume. They added the market could also bounce back during the day, if the U.S. opening will allow it. * General Index was down 3.06 points, or 0.49 pct, to 624.15 * Ibex-35 shed 22.7 points, or 0.32 pct, to 7,141.96 * Telefonica was losing 20 pesetas to 4,550 pesetas, with Repsol 20 pesetas 6,460 pesetas.
With domestic funds still looking to buy, banks stand to gain even after this year's spectacular run, dealers said.
"We're looking at very strong first half earnings for both Santander and BBV, with both up to ten percent below their fair value even at these levels," said a Benito y Monjardin dealer.
Conversely utilities are still weighed down by uncertainties over the deregulation of the market, tariffs and lower rainfall, although Endesa should be bolstered by the autumn public offer.
Endesa rose 50 pesetas to 12,450 and Iberdrola added 5 pesetas to 1,830.
